agent_explanation: Token-identity detector for the 'range' word-piece WITHOUT a leading space: the bare token 'range' (glued to a preceding hyphen, underscore, dot, bracket, quote, slash or word piece, e.g. 'long-range', 'out-of-range', 'get_range', 'x.range', 'xrange', 'Arrange') fires at ~10-13 (about 0.8-1.1x max), glued 'ranged' (e.g. 'free-ranged') ~8, and glued capitalised 'Range' (e.g. 'AddRange', 'DateRange', 'mode="RangeS-U"', line-initial after a newline) ~4.5-7; the spaced word ' Range' gives only a weak ~2.5-3.5 (near the 0.25x line), ' ranged' ~0.7-2.8 (usually below the line), and the ordinary spaced lowercase ' range' / ' ranges' / ' ranging' give exactly 0. Everything else (including 'orange', 'strange', 'Ranger') is 0, so there is no floor: prompts without a range token are inactive, and a range token as the very first token of the text is damped (bare 'range' ~5, 'Range' 0).
neuronpedia_explanation: references to long-range capabilities

agent_explanation: A token-identity detector for the space-prefixed two-digit number token ' 39' (strongest, ~0.8-0.95 of max) and, more weakly, ' 38' (~0.5-0.8), ' 48'/' 49' (~0.3-0.5) and ' 36' (~0.35); it fires on that number token itself in any context (ages, counts, percentages, arithmetic) and is near zero (<0.2 of max) on every other token, including other two-digit numbers (' 29', ' 31', ' 37', ' 40', ' 47', ' 93'), multi-digit tokens containing 39 (' 390', ' 1939'), the spelled-out 'thirty-nine', and the no-space '39' token. There is no floor: prompts without one of these number tokens stay below 0.25 of max.
neuronpedia_explanation: references to the number 39

agent_explanation: A near token-identity detector for the word ' passionate' (and less so ' passionately') used as a mid-text adjective, in any frame ('is passionate', 'a passionate man', 'The passionate debate'), at 0.6-1.0x max; a few other devotion/care trait words ' compassionate', ' caring', ' loving', ' fervent', ' enthusiastic', ' knowledgeable', ' avid', ' ardent', ' thoughtful' give weak activity (~0.2-0.45x max), while near-synonyms such as ' excited', ' eager', ' devoted', ' dedicated', ' kind', ' warm', ' loyal', ' empathetic', the noun ' passion' and the verb ' cares' stay ~0. Nothing sets a floor: prompts without these words (including punctuation-only text) are silent, and the word is silent as the very first token of a prompt.
neuronpedia_explanation: expressions denoting enthusiasm or strong emotion

agent_explanation: Single-token lexical detector for the space-prefixed word token ' favorite' / ' favourite' (any case, e.g. ' Favorite'), firing strongly (~0.6-0.9 of max) on that token regardless of the preceding determiner or context, and moderately (~0.3-0.4 of max) on the plural ' favorites' / ' favourites'; it is essentially silent (<0.05 of max) on synonyms ('best', 'preferred', 'beloved', 'fave'), on related forms that split differently ('favorited', 'favoritism', 'favor', 'favorable'), split capitalised spellings such as ' Favourites' fire moderately on the 'avour' piece (~0.3 of max); it is silent on unspaced prompt-initial 'favorite', and on all other tokens, so there is no floor on prompts lacking the word.
neuronpedia_explanation: mentions of favorites or preferred items

agent_explanation: Fires inside news-report prose about entertainment, celebrity, tech or sports stories, peaking on the source-attribution slot of a reporting construction: the 'to'/'by'/'told' right before a named outlet or recipient ('confirmed to', 'reported by', 'a source told', 'picked up by'), the outlet name itself before a reporting verb ('Variety reported', 'ESPN reported'), 'exclusively', and to a lesser degree 'released/announced on <date>'. It is silent (0, no floor on BOS or the first token) on non-news text such as recipes, domestic narrative or everyday speech, and stays weak (under ~0.3 of max) on bare 'X told Y' or 'by' without a news-story context.
neuronpedia_explanation: references to production or behind-the-scenes details in filmmaking

agent_explanation: Fires on the word 'result' used as a VERB of causal outcome (' result', ' results', ' resulted', ' resulting', as in 'X will result in / resulted in / resulting in / results from Y'), peaking on that verb token itself (~0.65-0.9 of max) with zero on all surrounding tokens; the NOUN 'result(s)' ('the final result', 'test results', 'as a result') stays near 0, synonyms like 'cause'/'led to'/'produces' give 0, and the near-synonym verb ' stem(s)' gives only a moderate response (~0.3-0.4), with ' arises'/' consists' weaker still (~0.2). There is no activity floor: every other token, including the first, is 0.
neuronpedia_explanation: terms related to consequences or outcomes

agent_explanation: Fires on the word itself (strongest as an attributive modifier) when it names a sectarian, ethnic-insurgent or non-state armed-faction identity: Shiite, Sunni, Kurdish, Houthi, Salafi, separatist, insurgent, guerrilla, rebel (even non-political 'teenage rebel'), militant, militia, paramilitary, Islamist, jihadist, Maoist (roughly 0.5-1.2 x max), with weaker firing on extremist and on the following head noun (cleric, fighters, militia, group ~0.05-0.4). It stays at zero on mainstream religious or national identities (Muslim, Christian, Catholic, Jewish, Palestinian, Canadian), on neutral group words (opposition, student, government, advocacy), on 'Islamic State', and mostly on 'terrorist'/'armed'/'radical' (below 0.2); ordinary text has no floor (zero everywhere), and the effect is lexical, not dependent on Middle-East news context.
neuronpedia_explanation: references to rebel groups and military factions in conflict situations

agent_explanation: Fires on the first byte-token 'âĢ' (bytes E2 80) of a curly apostrophe/quote that directly follows a word, typically a pronoun before a contraction (they’ll, we’re, you’ve, doesn’t, company’s), but only when the document has already used curly apostrophes ’ at least ~3 times earlier (strength grows with the count and is highest after a pronoun; the first one or two ’ in a text, ’ after punctuation, and straight apostrophes stay ~0); a weaker secondary case is the middle fragment of a multi-token rare name or tag repeated many times in a list (e.g. 'vel' in a repeated 'Lavelle', 'MB' in repeated 'ITEMNMBR'). Everything else, including short texts with fewer than three prior curly apostrophes, is ~0, so there is no floor.
neuronpedia_explanation: proper nouns and specific identifiers, particularly related to places and names

agent_explanation: Fires on the grammatical subject (pronoun such as it/they/he/she/we, or a bare head noun like group/team/era/people/name) of a new clause in a dated past-tense chronicle (company/person/station history: founded, began, joined in YEAR), at the point where the next event verb is due, strongest right after a narrative sequencer (Then, Later, eventually, before, soon, However) and peaking again on an adverb between subject and verb (soon, now, quickly); it is near zero on determiners, adjectives, object/possessive pronouns (them, their), on subjects after 'Today,' or 'So,', in present-tense/habitual or recent everyday contexts (yesterday, last week, after lunch), and on any text lacking such a historical narrative (no floor at the first token).
neuronpedia_explanation: phrases related to company names and corporate actions

agent_explanation: Topic-gated context latent: once the preceding text has mentioned digital security/privacy concepts (encryption, cryptography, digital signatures, private keys, hackers/hacking, passwords, VPN, privacy, anonymity), it fires on the following tokens, peaking at clause-boundary and discourse tokens (' to', ' that', ' because', ' so', ',', '.', ' Now', 'In practice', 'However,') that continue the discussion; the security word itself scores low. With no such security/crypto mention earlier in the text it stays at ~0 on every token (there is no floor), and generic IT words like firewall/malware give only weak activity.
neuronpedia_explanation: references to online security and related vulnerabilities

agent_explanation: A lexical detector for the word 'reform' itself (the GPT-2 token ' reform', including as the stem of ' reform'+'er'), firing on that token in roughly 0.75-1.0 x max whenever it means deliberately improving an institution, policy or person (tax/ethics/prison reform, 'promised to reform the agency', reform school, a thief vowing to reform). It fires only weakly (~0.15-0.45) when ' reform' means physically re-forming ('clouds/droplets/crystals reform into...'), at about half strength on variants (' reforms' ~0.65, ' reforming' ~0.57, capitalised 'Reform'/'form' ~0.5, ' reformed' ~0.3), and faintly (<=0.3) on near-synonyms of institutional improvement (' overhaul', ' modernization', ' improvements', ' upgrade', 'reformation'); it is zero on every other token, including plain synonyms like improve, reshape, rules, cuts, funding.
neuronpedia_explanation: mentions of reform in various contexts

agent_explanation: Fires only on the token ' take'/' takes' when the immediately preceding word makes it read as a NOUN: right after a determiner, possessive or noun-modifier ('the take', 'his take on', 'your take', 'a hot take', 'in one take', 'double take'), reaching 0.65-1.1 x max. Verb uses after a pronoun, modal, 'to', imperative or sentence start ('I will take', 'They take', 'to take', 'Please take', 'Take the') stay near 0, verb 'take' right after a plural noun subject ('the kids take', 'the fellas take') is weak (about 0.2-0.4 x max), and every other token (including 'took', 'taken', 'view', 'mistake', 'intake') is 0, so there is no floor on prompts without ' take'.
neuronpedia_explanation: various interpretations or perspectives on a subject

agent_explanation: Fires on the noun ' health' / ' Health' (weakly ' fitness', ' healthcare') when it stands as a bare head noun directly after a determiner, possessive, 'of', 'other' or a generic/evaluative adjective (e.g. 'protect the health of', 'the best health care', 'other health professionals', 'Department of Health'), and is near-silent when the immediately preceding word is a domain-specifying modifier that forms a fixed compound with it ('mental', 'human', 'animal', 'reproductive', 'occupational', 'general', 'World Health'); it never fires on related words such as 'medical', 'safety', 'care' or 'wealth'.
neuronpedia_explanation: terms related to healthcare topics

agent_explanation: Fires on the token ' per' when it immediately follows a bare numeric quantity (digits, decimals strongest, '%', '$' amounts, or a number word), forming a rate/ratio like '2.9 per 1000', '4.9 per cent', '$1.25 per share', '7% per year'; strongest in rate, price, dividend or percentage contexts and weak (<0.3 of max) in speed/score contexts like '60 per hour'. It is silent on every other token (no floor), on ' per' after a noun or unit ('miles per hour', 'deaths per', 'listed per person', 'as per'), and on 'percent'/'%' alone.
neuronpedia_explanation: instances of percentages

agent_explanation: Fires only on a compound-joining hyphen (more weakly '/' or '_') placed right after a standalone word that is the first part of a noun-first compound. It is strongest (~0.8-1.0 x max) when that word is lowercase ' time'/' times' ('time-consuming', 'time-dependent', 'time-shift', 'time-saving', 'time-out'). It is moderate (~0.2-0.5 x max) after other quantity/resource nouns such as life, cost, age, date, dose, price, money ('life-time', 'cost-effective', 'age-dependent'), and weaker for capitalized sentence-initial 'Time-' or for 'time/' and 'microtime_'. It is zero everywhere else: on the following word, on hyphens after adjectives/adverbs or other first elements (well-, high-, part-, full-, real-, long-, labor-, data-, user-, very-), on hyphens after compounds where 'time' is the second element ('real-time', 'part-time'), on spaced dashes, and on every other token, so ordinary prose without such a compound has no activity floor.
neuronpedia_explanation: phrases related to time management issues

agent_explanation: Fires on a bare single-digit numeral token ' 1' (strongest, ~0.7-1.0 of max) or ' 2' (~0.4-0.5; ' 3' and higher digits weak, ' 7'/' 9' near zero) when it directly follows a quantity hedge or bound such as 'more/fewer than', 'over', 'at least', 'up to', 'nearly', 'almost', 'about', 'approximately', 'roughly' or 'a total of' (milder after 'by', 'exactly', 'at most'), i.e. the leading digit of an approximate or bounded quantity like 'more than 1 year' or 'nearly 1,000'. It is silent on the same digit with no preceding quantifier ('lost 1,000 items', 'Chapter 1', 'page 1', '1999'), on spelled-out or multi-digit-token numbers ('a mile', ' 10', ' 100'), on all other tokens, and there is no floor on the first token or on prompts without such a numeral.
neuronpedia_explanation: phrases indicating numerical quantities or statistics related to "more than one."

agent_explanation: Fires on the first word right after an example-introducing word: 'including', 'include(s/d)' used to introduce members of a set, or 'such as'. It is strongest (about 0.7-1.0 x max) when that word is a determiner or pronoun ('the', 'a', 'this', 'those', 'your'), weaker (about 0.3-0.5) on a bare noun or name ('Paris') and on weaker introducers ('like', 'especially', 'notably', 'for example', 'excluding'), and decays over the following words. It is silent (0) on the same word after non-exemplifying connectives ('and', 'with', 'despite', 'are', 'involve', 'contains'), and on ordinary text with no such word the floor is 0.
neuronpedia_explanation: references to reforms and their associated elements

agent_explanation: Fires on the second word of a noun phrase (the pre-head slot right after 'the'/'some'/'all') when that phrase is the object of a verb of examining, presenting or selecting (look at, list, describe, examine, review, discuss, identify, rank, determine, calculate, study, compare, highlight, show you) or of a presentational question/frame ('What is the', 'Here is the'), and the word picks items out of a set: superlative or ranking modifiers (best, greatest, highest, leading, main, top, key, latest, first, favorite, most) are strongest, and generic 'new' or a second determiner ('all the', 'some of the') are moderate. It stays near zero on the bare determiner and the head noun, on descriptive adjectives (young, red), and when the same phrase follows a physical-action verb (eat, buy, kick) or a plain copula ('He was the best', 'It is the best').
neuronpedia_explanation: references to lists or enumerations of items or facts

agent_explanation: Fires on the determiner (mostly ' the'; weaker on ' a', ' my', ' every', ' this') that directly follows a directional preposition/particle (to, on, off, in, into, out of, up to) governed by a light motion or reaching verb, i.e. the slot naming the destination in 'get/got to the', 'come to the', 'go/went to the', 'got on/off the', 'taken to the', 'up to the task', 'look in the', 'get out of the'; 'get/got' gives the strongest activation (often above the scan max) and come/go/take/run next. It is zero on every other token (including the first token, so there is no floor), zero when the preposition follows a non-motion verb (talked to, listened to, sat on, belongs to, arrived at, welcome to, according to, close to) or a non-directional preposition (from, with, over), and weak (<0.45 of max) for manner-of-motion verbs like walked/drove.
neuronpedia_explanation: occurrences of the word "the" and phrases indicating direction or transition

agent_explanation: Fires only on the final 't' of an n't negation contraction spelled with the curly Unicode apostrophe (’, two byte tokens), strongest for present-tense do-support 'don’t'/'doesn’t' after a pronoun subject (I/We/She, ~0.7-0.9 of max) and weaker after noun subjects or for didn’t/haven’t/aren’t (~0.2-0.4), near zero for won’t/isn’t/weren’t/imperative 'Don’t', and zero for wasn’t/couldn’t, for the bare ’ or other ’ contractions (’s, ’m), and for uncontracted 'do not'. The ASCII apostrophe ('t, at most ~0.1) and the apostrophe-less ' dont' (~0.2) give only weak activation.
neuronpedia_explanation: the presence of the phrase "I don't" or its variations

agent_explanation: A context-independent detector of the single GPT-2 token for Apple's mobile OS name 'iOS' (' iOS' or bare 'iOS' as in '[iOS]' / '(iOS)'), firing near max (~0.85-1.1x) on that token in any sentence position except the very first token of the text, and zero on all other tokens; weak offshoots are other Apple OS names, ' macOS' (~0.4x) and the ' X' of 'OS X' (~0.25x, borderline), while spellings that split differently ('IOS', 'ios'), Android, Windows, Linux, iPhone, Safari and C++ stay below 0.12x, so a text with no iOS/macOS/OS X token has no activity floor and is predicted inactive.
neuronpedia_explanation: references to different versions of iOS

agent_explanation: Fires on the head word of an abstract noun or predicate naming a diffuse, ongoing state of strain, agitation or instability, especially between parties: tension(s) is by far the strongest (about 5 bare, about 10 after framings like 'amid rising ... with'), and strain, friction, turmoil, unrest, chaos, instability, volatility, animosity, unease, turbulence, trouble, discord, 'tense' and 'strained' are moderate (2-7). It stays near zero on discrete hostile events (war, fight, fighting, row), on neutral or positive nouns in the same slot (trade, changes, growth, cooperation, peace), and on 'trouble' meaning difficulty ('had trouble sleeping'). Preceding context that makes the strain social rather than mechanical raises it ('rivals felt rising tension' about 6.7 vs 'steel wire felt rising tension' about 1.7).
neuronpedia_explanation: references to rising tensions or conflicts

agent_explanation: Fires on a number token (or the first piece of a split number) that a dating context marks as a past point or age in time -- after 'dates back/from/to', 'as far back as', 'since', 'built/erected in', 'aged', or inside a parenthetical era range like '(794-1185)' -- strongest for pre-modern years and archaeological spans (800, 1200, 2,000 years, 65 million years: ~0.5-0.9 of max), weak for modern years (1900+, ~0-0.2) and also weakly on an approximator ('around', 'about') right after a dating verb; it is ~0 on the same numbers used as counts, prices, measurements, room or version numbers, on plain 'X years ago' without a dating verb, and on any text without numbers (no floor).
neuronpedia_explanation: numerals and historical dates

agent_explanation: Fires on a coordinating token (' and', ' or', ' &', ' /', weaker on ',') that immediately follows a word from the law/legal-justice field (law, laws, Law, legal, legally, statutory, statute, legislation, legislative, constitutional, criminal, civil, court, judicial, justice, rights, lawyers, Securities, Competition, tax), i.e. coordinating that legal term with a following conjunct (e.g. 'law or agreed', 'law and economics', 'statutory and constitutional', 'Securities and Exchange'); a few non-legal first conjuncts also trigger it (' Bill' as in 'Bill & Melinda', ' death', 'men and women'). It is silent on the same conjunction after ordinary words (music, apples, food, science, Health, government), on non-coordinating words after legal terms ('law but', 'law.'), on clause-level 'and' after a verb phrase ('broke the law and ran'), and on every other token, so prompts without such a conjunction stay at 0.
neuronpedia_explanation: instances of the word "Law" and its associations in various contexts

agent_explanation: Fires on an evaluative quality adjective (by far most strongly ' good'/' Good'; weaker for ' bad', ' great', ' successful', ' poor', ' excellent', ' happy', ' decent', ' strong') when it sits in a generic or normative frame about what makes something a good instance of its kind, e.g. 'the key/secret to a good X', 'what makes a good X', 'a/every good X should/must', 'to be/do a good X', 'how to become a good X', 'you need a good X', 'Good food tastes better'. It stays near zero on the same adjective when it evaluates a particular, episodic referent ('She was a good teacher', 'It was a good movie', 'He did a good job', 'had a good time'), in predicate position ('the food was good'), in fixed phrases ('a good idea', 'Good morning'), and on non-evaluative adjectives (new, long, famous, local).
neuronpedia_explanation: instances of the word "good" and its variations in the context of qualities or attributes

agent_explanation: Fires on the preposition that introduces the penalty right after a criminal-sentencing verb: near max on ' to' in 'sentenced/resentenced (him) to' (also with an adverbial in between, e.g. 'sentenced yesterday to'), about 0.6x on 'condemned to', about 0.4-0.5x on 'ordered to' and 'a sentence of'; it stays below 0.25x on ' to'/'for'/'with' after other passive verbs (sent, exiled, deported, confined, promoted, assigned, doomed, forced, jailed for, punished with, sentenced for). It is zero on all other tokens, including the sentencing verb itself and any non-sentencing ' to', so there is no floor on ordinary text.
neuronpedia_explanation: phrases related to sentencing and prison terms

agent_explanation: Fires only on the token 'let'/'Let'/' let'/' Let' itself (never on the following tokens, and zero on everything else including 'Here', 'If', 'Suppose', 'var') when it opens a clause or statement: strongest for line-initial math 'Let x be/= ...' after a newline and code declarations ('let name: String', 'let b = 2'), moderate for imperative 'Let's/Let me/Let us' after a sentence boundary or comma; weak or zero for embedded verb uses ('she let me', 'would let', 'should let it go'). It is zero when 'Let' is the very first token of the prompt, so prompts without a later clause-opening 'let' have no activity floor.
neuronpedia_explanation: instances of the word "Let."

agent_explanation: Fires on the token of an 'affect'-class verb (affect/affects/affected/affecting, impact, effect used as a verb, and more weakly influence, impair, hurt, harm, alter, damage) when it is read as an active transitive verb right after its subject or a modal/auxiliary (e.g. 'X may affect', 'which affected', 'will impact', 'drought affected areas'); strongest for affect/impact (~0.8-1.1 x max), ~0.4-0.55 for influence/impair/hurt/harm, ~0.3 for alter/damage. It is near zero for noun uses after a determiner ('an impact on', 'the impact of', 'an effect'), passive or adjectival participles ('were affected by', 'the affected patients', 'deeply affected'), neutral or positive verbs (help, cover, boost, protect, change, determine), and every other token, so there is no floor on prompts lacking such a verb.
neuronpedia_explanation: words related to influence or consequences

agent_explanation: Fires on the space-less GPT-2 token 'if' or 'IF' (the bare subword, not ' if'), strongest (0.7-0.95 of max) when it is a word-internal fragment continuing a preceding letter piece (Mult|if|lori, Nutr|if|en, CAL|IF|ORNIA, B|if|urcation, ang|ust|if|olia), moderate (~0.5-0.6) for combat|if, int|if|ada, MOD|IF|Y and code 'if' right after a tab, weak (<0.25) after '#' or 'el' and on space-prefixed ' if' before an unseen subword like 'rames'; it is silent on the English conjunction ' if'/' If', on 'if' as the first token of a prompt or after ';', and on words that never produce a bare 'if' token (difference, California, beautiful, pacific), so ordinary text has no activity floor.
neuronpedia_explanation: occurrences of the word "if."

agent_explanation: Fires on the determiner that opens a noun phrase which is the object of a preposition or verb in mid-sentence, mainly 'the' and also possessives (my/his/their/'s), demonstratives and all/a/any, often with a weaker echo on a following adjective such as 'last' or 'same'. It is strongest after relational or compound prepositions and phrases ('on the back of the', 'outside of the', 'next to/beside the', 'at the edge/heart of the', 'produced for the', 'take a look at my', 'keeps making the'). It is weak or zero after plain 'on/in/to the', on sentence-initial subject determiners, on bare-noun or numeral objects ('of dense forest', 'two lamps') and on content words; there is no floor: the first token and determiner-free text read 0.
neuronpedia_explanation: articles and common expressions used in descriptions

agent_explanation: Fires on the head noun ' government' (space-prefixed; ' Government' about half as strong) when it names the national/central state as an acting party, e.g. 'the (federal) government', strongest (5-10) as a party in legal or policy dispute clauses like 'argues that the government ...', and weaker (1.5-3.5) on other national state-authority nouns used the same way (' administration', ' Congress', ' agency', ' authorities', ' CIA', ' State', ' officials', ' court' after 'trial'). It is near zero on every other token (no floor), on 'local government', ' governor', private parties (company, contractor, neighbors, police), the bare modifier ' federal', and the employer sense 'works for the government'.
neuronpedia_explanation: references to the federal government

agent_explanation: Fires on the token that completes the name of a commercial business, at the end of a multi-token company name (Goldman [[Sachs]], General [[Motors]], Ford Motor [[Company]], Smith & [[Sons]], Johnson & [[Johnson]], Acme [[Corporation]]/Inc[[.]], Hers[[hey]], KPM[[G]], CI[[BC]], Al[[ibaba]], the autom[[aker]]), and on a possessive 's directly after such a name. It is silent on person names, places, non-commercial institutions (United Nations, Harvard), lowercase descriptors ('Smith & sons'), very famous single-token brands (Microsoft, Google, Apple, Ford), and every token of plain text has a floor of 0 (no first-token or positional activity).
neuronpedia_explanation: proper nouns related to companies or brands

agent_explanation: Fires on a Latinate verb-stem token, mostly ones ending in -ct/-t/-pt or 'Conquer' (Detect, Collect, Protect, sculpt, select, induct, elect, conserv, creat, Execut), when the context puts that stem in a noun or modifier slot, e.g. after a determiner, a title like Lord, a modifier noun or adjective, or inside a code identifier. In that slot the stem has to be the start of a derived word ending in -or/-ors (also -ive, -ion, -ing). It is near zero for the same stem in a verb slot (after to, will, a subject pronoun) and for stems that take other agent suffixes (Command, Defend, build, paint), and its decoder promotes 'or', 'ors', 'orship', 'ive'.
neuronpedia_explanation: forms of the word "collect" and related terms indicating aggregation or collection

agent_explanation: Fires on a time-unit noun (year(s), month(s), week(s), day(s), season, decade, hour, also game(s)/time when used as a count of periods) that closes a span phrase measuring how long a status, trend, ranking or record has held, as in news/statistics framing: 'for the third consecutive year', 'lowest level in four years', 'first sighting in 26 years', 'stock fell for a fifth day', 'was top for three years'. It stays at zero on every other token (no floor on any prompt), on non-time nouns in the same slot ('in 26 rooms'), and on plain durations of a personal activity or age/time-reference uses ('lived there for three years', 'lasted two hours', '26 years old', 'next year', 'years ago' outside a record context).
neuronpedia_explanation: sequences of time-related occurrences or trends

agent_explanation: Fires on the token right before a slot where a money noun (funds, funding, budget, cost, grants, money, pay) is the likely next word, i.e. when the preceding context is about paying, funding, spending, debt or campaign finance and the current word opens that slot ("without [extra] funding", "his [campaign] funds", "the [total] cost", "ability [to] pay", "Home [Office] grants", "with her [own] money", "the agency['s] budget"). The same frame with the money cue swapped for a non-financial word (kids, staffed, painted, praised) stays near 0, apart from a few budget-like modifiers (annual, yearly, extra) that reach about 0.5 x max even on their own. There is no baseline floor: ordinary non-financial text is 0 at every token, including the first.
neuronpedia_explanation: references to financial aspects and responsibilities

agent_explanation: Fires on a restrictive relative pronoun (' that', less on ' which'/' who', with no comma before it) that opens a relative clause on an indefinite noun phrase naming something wanted, needed, sought or being made (object of want/need/look for/create/build/develop/make/craft, e.g. 'I want a car[[ that]]', 'to develop analgesics[[ that]]'), i.e. a clause about the required properties of a not-yet-existing or hypothetical thing. It is weak (under ~0.2 of max) when the head noun is an existing referent (saw/have/used/found/heard a ...), definite ('the car that' about half), the sentence subject ('The man that came'), or the clause is non-restrictive (', which'), and silent for complementizer or conjunction 'that' ('hope that', 'so that', 'the fact that') and for demonstrative 'That'.
neuronpedia_explanation: proposals for significant societal changes or systems
